thread:
harper: Heads-up — another wave of truncated streaming responses (HTTP 206) on /v1/stream/chat around 05:22 UTC. ~830 requests, concentrated in us-east-1 and ap-northeast-1. Traces show runtime closing mid-chunk during large emits.

leo: Can you paste a couple of samples and whether any autoscaler events line up?

harper: Samples: 
```
2026-10-09T05:22:14Z req=zz9f region=us-east status=206 emit_bytes=144 ERR=runtime:emit-interrupted; close=EOF
2026-10-09T05:23:01Z req=zz9g region=ap-northeast status=206 emit_bytes=28 ERR=proxy:drain-initiated
```

anya: ops-bot create sev3 and assign owners. This is starting to look like a recurring systemic issue.

ops-bot: INCIDENT_CREATED: #inc-2026-10-streaming-truncation-pattern (sev3) — responders: @harper @leo @anya

natalie: Quick proposal for durable remediation and follow-ups: short-term: align timeouts, add Retry-After on forced disconnects, throttle noisy reconnect loops. Medium-term: emit final control frames that indicate forced truncation and add a `partial_tag` so analytics exclude expected truncations. Long-term: implement drain-aware stream handoff and best-effort resume tokens in the client SDKs. Owners?

leo: I'll take timeout alignment and Retry-After semantics at the proxy. Plan: harmonize upstream/downstream idle to 45s for canary pool (a bit longer for large emits), add explicit Retry-After with backoff guidance. ETA config roll (canary): 24h.

anya: I'll own runtime changes: BestEffortFlush on drain with configurable grace (default 7s) and emit a final control event `event:stream_truncated reason=drain` with `partial_tag=forced_drain`. PR ETA: 72h.

prashant: I'll prototype the drain-aware handoff: when a pod is draining, try to transfer active streams to a warm standby on the same node group by issuing a short-lived resume token to clients. If resume succeeds, client reconnect will continue from last ack; otherwise runtime emits `partial_tag=forced_drain`. This is experimental but could drastically reduce user-facing partials. Prototype ETA: 2 weeks.

harper: Nice. Please ensure the resume token approach is opt-in and respects security (short TTL, single-use). We also need server-side dedup / idempotency if clients retry.

natalie: Observability work: add `stream_state` timeline events (OPEN, FIRST_BYTE, LAST_BYTE, DRAIN_NOTICE, RESUME_ATTEMPT, CLOSE_REASON) and `partial_tag` in traces and logs. Extend trace retention for streaming traces to 30d to ease forensic joins. Owner:@natalie ETA: 5 days for metrics & dashboard.

leo: Also adding a short-term mitigant: edge throttle for noisy clients (>50 short streams/min) returning 429+Retry-After. Owner:@leo ETA: 48h. We'll include client guidance for exponential backoff with jitter.

anya: Test plan: unit tests for BestEffortFlush success/fail, integration harness to simulate mid-stream drain + network jitter, and a 3h staging run at 50% load. Acceptance: partial_rate < 0.15% during the run.

prashant: For the resume token prototype I'll add a proof-of-concept to the client SDKs (python/ts) that accepts a resume token and attempts a single resumptive reconnect. Fallback remains safe (full reconnect). We'll include a flag to disable in enterprise/private deployments.

natalie: Alerting: create a short-lived alert (partial_rate > 0.4% over 5m) and a weekly trend job that emails eng if region-level 90-day delta > 20%. Also create a dashboard showing partial_rate vs pod_evictions and drain counts.

harper: Adding action items to tracker now: 
1) runtime: BestEffortFlush + final control frame + partial_tag (owner:@anya) — due: 2026-10-12
2) proxy: timeout harmonization + Retry-After header + edge throttle (owner:@leo) — due: 2026-10-11
3) observability: stream_state timeline + partial_tag + 30d retention (owner:@natalie) — due: 2026-10-14
4) SDK: resume token POC + client guidance (owner:@prashant) — due: 2026-10-25
5) tests & staging: reproduce and acceptance runs (owner:@anya/@prashant) — due: 2026-10-15

leo: Rolling a conservative canary for timeout changes (5% traffic) now; will monitor partial_rate and KPS for 6h. Stop condition: partial_rate > 0.3% for 2h.

ops-bot: Canaries started for timeout-harmonization (canary-id: cny-1888-01).

prashant: Note on security — resume tokens will be HMAC-signed with a short TTL (default 10s) and single-use. Will add token shape to design doc.

harper: Customer comms: I'll draft a short note for affected tenants explaining mitigations and recommended client backoff patterns. We'll avoid detailed internals. ETA: 48h.

natalie: On-call grep snippet for investigations: 
```
jq -r '.events[] | select(.status==206) | [.req,.region,.partial_tag,.stream_state,.close_reason] | @tsv' streaming-traces.ndjson | rg "drain|forced_drain|resume"
```

anya: I'll push the BestEffortFlush PR to staging today and wire the final control frame. Will add unit tests and the reproduction harness artifacts.

leo: Early canary shows a small drop in partials for the first 30m. Continuing to watch.

harper: Scheduling a follow-up sync Tue 14:00 UTC to review PRs, canary metrics, and decide whether to proceed to wider rollout. If any owner misses a due date, escalate to eng leads. :spiral_calendar:

ops-bot: INCIDENT_RESOLVED: #inc-2026-10-streaming-truncation-pattern (informational) — mitigation plan recorded; long-term work in trackers, canary monitoring ongoing.
